quote.translation: Teleological contingency readily enters into heterogeneous combination with causal necessity, and causal necessity in turn, through homogeneous combination, combines with teleological necessity; this "necessity-contingency" complex, having acquired a transcendence of the actual through the enormity of the matter itself, is nothing other than fate.

regions.text: その際、因果的必然と目的々必然との同種結合は次のやうな意味でなされる。

quote.translation: The homogeneous combination of causal necessity and teleological necessity is made here in the following sense.

regions.text: 目的性は未來によつて現在を決定するものとして曩にも云つたやうに（六八夏参照）意識を豫想してゐる。しかし意識と無意識との間には段階約な通路が開けてるる。意識はこの通路を通つて無意識へ韓する。

quote.translation: Purposiveness, as what determines the present through the future, presupposes consciousness, as I said earlier (see p. 68), but between consciousness and the unconscious there opens a graded passage, and through this passage consciousness turns into the unconscious.

regions.text: 斯くして目前必然は因果必然と結合し、因果的必然は目々必然と結合するのである。

quote.translation: In this way teleological necessity combines with causal necessity, and causal necessity with teleological necessity.

regions.text: ディオゲネス・ラェルテ「オスはストア派の説として「一切は運命（sipappesn）によつて起る。さうして運命とは存在者の原風（airia）もしくは世界がそれによつて運行する理型（aoyos）である」BiogenesLaertiosVI,15）と云つてるる。

quote.translation: Diogenes Laertius reports as a Stoic doctrine that "all things come about by fate (εἱμαρμένη), and fate is the cause (αἰτία) of existents, or the reason (λόγος) by which the world proceeds" (Diogenes Laertios, VII, 149), and there is no harm in seeing here two moments contained within fate, teleological necessity as "reason" and causal necessity as "cause".

regions.text: この場合、運命の中には「理性」としての目時々必然性と原因」としての因果的必然性との二つの契機が含まれてゐると見て差支ないであらう。

quote.translation: Causal necessity and teleological necessity, at any rate, enter into homogeneous combination.

regions.text: ともかくも因果約必然と目約々必然とは同種結合をする。なほ運命の概念にあつて、目々偶然と目々必然こが結合してゐるのは如何なる意味かといふに前者は人間實の地平に於ける目性に關し、後者は超越的目性に開してるるのである。

quote.translation: As for what it means that teleological contingency and teleological necessity are combined in the concept of fate, the former concerns purposiveness on the horizon of human Existenz, whilst the latter concerns transcendent purposiveness.

regions.text: 要するに、目々偶然が因果必然と結合し更にその媒介によつて目々必然と結合し、「必然

quote.translation: Fate, in short, is teleological contingency that combines with causal necessity and, through that mediation, with teleological necessity as well, and which, as the necessary- contingent, is at once pushed away into the infinitely distant and drawn into the infinitely near.
